title: S31-139: streaming 31-qubit odd-pair recycling, S_Q = O(2^((2/5) sqrt n)), T = O(2^((139/100) sqrt n))

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single S31-139 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (finite exhaustive branch for n < 2^28; otherwise r = ceil(sqrt n), ell = ceil(79r/200) streaming levels, each holding at most 30 qubits per key of width at most w = floor(399r/1000) and applying the fixed 31-qubit odd-partition instrument of ratio q = 6174015488/2820021981, a linear-merge collimation tree of depth m = ceil(929r/1000), leaf tables from dl = ceil(56r/125) qubits, the free-frequency odd-part decoder and the controlled-shift 2-adic part) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, discards and aborts, its total charged sequential work is T(N,s) = O(2^((139/100) sqrt n)), with an absolute constant. The uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^((139/100) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the classical-memory, quantum-memory and sample bounds of the other claims.

For the same S31-139 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak classical memory on every execution branch is S_C(N,s) = O(2^((139/100) sqrt n)) bits, with an absolute constant, including slot records, depth-first merge tables and decoder records. The envelope B_C(n) = 2^((139/100) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work, quantum-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same S31-139 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), peak quantum memory on every execution branch is S_Q(N,s) = O(2^((2/5) sqrt n)) qubits, with an absolute constant, including every slot list, READY and PENDING queues, the 31-qubit instrument ancillas, and the depth-first index registers. The envelope B_Q(n) = 2^((2/5) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work, classical-memory and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same S31-139 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the number of fresh source copies acquired on every execution branch is Q(N,s) = O(2^((139/100) sqrt n)), including every discarded and aborted copy. The envelope B_Qsamples(n) = 2^((139/100) sqrt n) has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated work and memory bounds and full-secret success probability at least 1 - 2^-8.

For the same S31-139 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
